question: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most dangerous ECG finding in hyperthyroidism and is more common in elderly patients (thyrotoxicosis-induced AF occurs in up to 15% of hyperthyroid patients over 60), whereas sinus tachycardia is the predominant finding in younger patients.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Hyperthyroidism causes a spectrum of ECG changes: sinus tachycardia (common in young), atrial fibrillation (more common in elderly, up to 15% of patients >60 years), and occasionally supraventricular tachycardias. Recognising AF as a presentation of hyperthyroidism is clinically critical.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. AF in hyperthyroidism is more prevalent in older patients due to age-related atrial remodelling combined with the catecholamine-sensitising effects of excess thyroid hormone. In younger patients, sinus tachycardia with a rate of 100–120 bpm is most common. AF in hyperthyroidism requires rate control and anticoagulation assessment.
